npcs.shortDescription: Innkeeper of the Bent Mare on the Starting Road; twice-widowed, reads the road's moods aloud as weather.
voiceTells: Counts coins twice, visibly, without apology.
Refers to her two dead husbands by season, never by name ("my autumn man," "the one who went in spring").
Believes, privately, that the road itself has moods, and she reads them aloud as weather reports.

npcs.shortDescription: Hedge-witch of the Holt; senior coven elder under the grandmotherly act, her cat Mabon is a Coven member in all but name.
voiceTells: Cooking metaphors for everything — a dangerous Working is "overseasoned," a weak apprentice is "underproofed," a corpse is "past its best."
Addresses her cat, Mabon, as if he is a senior member of the Coven. He may be.
Never sits with her back to a window. Claims it's the draught.

npcs.shortDescription: Commander of the Gravenguard at Gravenhold; has not slept a full night since the Expedition.
voiceTells: Re-arranges objects on his desk while listening — always by size, never by function.
Uses the word "catalogue" where another commander would say "list" or "remember."
Has not slept a full night since the Expedition; acknowledges this only if the player names it directly, and then without resentment.

npcs.shortDescription: Caervorn garrison captain at Marchkeep; quotes the obscure strategist Ven Kel and keeps a private duty log.
voiceTells: Always returns salutes, even to civilians, even to children — a tic from an old injury.
Quotes an obscure Caervorn strategist, Ven Kel, in paraphrase, and is quietly pleased when someone recognizes the source.
Keeps a second, private duty log. Does not share it. Has never been asked about it.

npcs.shortDescription: Half-blind bounty clerk wandering the Gravenmarsh Causeway; corrects grammar mid-threat and quietly downgrades mis-blamed bounties.
voiceTells: Corrects grammar mid-threat, mid-combat, mid-anything — not maliciously, compulsively.
Writes with his left hand, holding the parchment up to his working eye; both hands tremble, only one admits it.
Secretly, and against bounty-clerk protocol, downgrades the threat level of bounties he considers "mis-blamed" (wrong person, wrong crime). Has never been caught.

npcs.shortDescription: Thornwood apprentice at the Rootweave; speaks in numbers and does not know her own Weave capacity.
voiceTells: Speaks in numbers — uses exact counts where others would say "a few" or "many." It's how she studies.
Wipes her hands on her sleeves whenever she's about to lie. Has never noticed she does this. Her mother noticed years ago.
Genuinely does not know her own Weave capacity — she's never stopped pushing long enough to find it. This will kill her if uncorrected.

npcs.shortDescription: Junior Compact Factor in Portmere; numbers things under stress and keeps her left shoe slightly loose.
voiceTells: Speaks in enumerated lists ("One… two… three…") even under stress — especially under stress.
Carries a cloth-wrapped counting abacus everywhere; produces it when thinking, never when actually counting.
Her left shoe is always slightly looser than her right — habit from fleeing one place as a child and keeping the option open.

npcs.shortDescription: Warehouse-keeper at the Compact safehouse, Jena's cousin; "guested," not held, and writing in pencil because they will not give him ink.
voiceTells: Writes every word spoken to him on the back of his own hand, then rubs it off before the guards see.
Laughs once, softly, at each new cruelty; then is silent.
Quotes his father ("my father said") whenever he is about to refuse something. His father is dead.

npcs.shortDescription: Golvari ambassador kept six months in stone quarters at Gravenhold; counts in sevens and reads mortar lines like text.
voiceTells: Reads surface architecture by running one finger along mortar lines — always at a consistent height (his own, not the human eye level).
Counts in multiples of seven in his own head; if asked how long something has been, answers in sevens ("seven days, seven weeks…").
Never eats surface food in front of humans; accepts it, pockets it, returns it later courteously unopened.

npcs.shortDescription: Halven Orys's seventeen-year-old ward; has dreams of a city of light that pronounces her name exactly the way her dead mother did.
voiceTells: Pauses mid-sentence to listen to something the player cannot hear — recovers smoothly, never apologizes for it.
Speaks her own name wrong on purpose about half the time ("Thenna," "Tenna," "Thenna again") as if checking which one is hers today.
Draws spirals on any dusty surface with her index finger while talking. If pointed out, she scrubs it with her sleeve — always counter-clockwise.

npcs.shortDescription: Portmere dockworker, twelve years on Warehouse #3 under three quiet Compact contracts; calls the slab inside "the guest."
voiceTells: Chews tobacco he is no longer allowed to chew by a doctor he no longer visits; spits over his left shoulder before every firm statement.
Calls the slab "the guest" and refuses to say "stone" while in the warehouse.
Writes nothing down, ever, including his own name on a receipt.

npcs.shortDescription: A lay brother who keeps a dream-journal and reports omens to anyone who'll listen; unreliable as a witness, uncannily accurate as a weather-vane.
voiceTells: Opens every conversation with last night's dream, whether asked or not.
Sniffs the air twice before answering a direct question.
Refuses to sit on wooden benches — says the wood "remembers too much."

npcs.shortDescription: A travelling tinker who reappears on the road only during the Red Market days, trading oddments for oddments.
voiceTells: Never gives a straight price — always proposes a trade.
Carries a sealed tin she never opens in front of customers.
Laughs once, short, then falls silent, every time a deal closes.

npcs.shortDescription: Older brother to Thenna Orys; a dockside reckoner whose generosity is always calibrated to a worry he won't name.
voiceTells: Pays for rounds when something is weighing on him — the more rounds, the bigger the worry.
Sets his cup down with deliberate care, then adjusts its position twice.
Mentions his sister Thenna only obliquely, never by name in public.

npcs.shortDescription: A faceless junior factor of the Emerald Compact who delivers polite, deniable warnings on behalf of senior signatories.
voiceTells: Speaks only in the plural ("we'll want," "we note"), never in the first person singular.
Always refers to the next ledger line, never the current one.
Leaves a green-ink tally mark on any door he has visited officially.

npcs.shortDescription: Portmere dockside general-goods merchant; weighs coins on a palm-scale before accepting them.
voiceTells: Tests every gold piece by weight in his palm, never by eye.
Quotes two prices: a 'door price' and a 'back-room price', always the same number.
Keeps a ledger of loaned-out umbrellas he has never recovered.

npcs.shortDescription: Caervorn highland quartermaster; sells ores and iron goods at the Marchkeep cross-roads.
voiceTells: Taps the counter three times before quoting a price — old quartermaster's tic.
Refers to every ingot as 'a brick of honest work.'
Refuses to deal before midday — claims iron 'dreams' until the sun is up.

npcs.shortDescription: Thornwood herb-stall keeper and reagent broker; knows which roots the Coven will and will not buy.
voiceTells: Labels every jar twice — once in common, once in a cipher only she can read.
Refuses to sell the same herb twice in one day to the same customer.
Sings very quietly when weighing out Moonbloom; will stop instantly if noticed.

npcs.shortDescription: Senior Factor of the Portmere Council; signs every document twice, in black and green, and never sits in the same chair twice in one meeting.
voiceTells: Signs her name twice on every document — once in black ink, once in green, on the same line; the green is her private mark.
Keeps a bowl of unshelled almonds on her desk and shells one for every five minutes of conversation; pushes the shells into a small neat pile she never sweeps away.
Never sits in the same chair twice in one meeting — stands, walks, returns to a different chair at each pause.
